name: Write a first message from evidence
when: The founder wants to write to someone for the first time: a lead, an investor, a possible partner or hire.
procedure: Find one thing this person actually said or did in public: a post, a talk, a launch, a hire. Keep the link.
Open with it, quoted or named exactly, and say in one sentence why it made the founder write.
Say who the founder is and what they do in one sentence.
Make one ask that is easy to say yes to: a 15-minute call, one question answered, feedback on one thing.
Keep the whole message under 80 words, then run the "Humanize a draft" skill on it. The founder sends it by hand.
pitfalls: Flattery ("I love your work") is not evidence; name the specific thing.
Two asks in one message get neither answered.
Never invent a shared connection or a detail you did not read.
verify: The message is under 80 words, names one specific public thing the person said or did with its link, contains exactly one ask, and every claim in it is true.
